title: The Maccabean Martyrs
aka: the mother and her seven sons
lead: The old teacher Eleazar, seven brothers and their mother, put to death under the Greek king Antiochus IV, about 167 BC, for refusing to eat pork against the law of Moses. 2 Maccabees 6:18-7:42 tells their deaths, 4 Maccabees builds a whole speech on them, Meyer and the Expositor's Greek Testament take Hebrews 11:35 as an allusion to them, and the Orthodox Church keeps them as saints, the Holy Maccabees, on 1 August (OCA).

sections.b: 2 Maccabees names only Eleazar, "one of the foremost scribes" (2 Maccabees 6:18); the brothers and their mother are unnamed, and no place is given. 4 Maccabees makes Eleazar a priest (4 Maccabees 5:4) and imagines their tomb inscribed: "Here an old priest is buried, with an old woman and seven sons" (4 Maccabees 17:9). Later tradition gave them names: the Orthodox Church calls the mother Solomonia and the brothers Abim, Antonius, Gurias, Eleazar, Eusebonus, Alimus and Marcellus, and says Eleazar died at Jerusalem and the seven were tried at Antioch (OCA). The medieval Hebrew Josippon calls the mother Hannah, and Erasmus's Latin paraphrase calls her Solomona (Townshend).

Their shrine at Antioch was "first Jewish and later Christian" (De Young). Gregory of Nazianzus and John Chrysostom preached on them, and Townshend notes that they were honored in the West too, by Augustine and Leo the Great and in the calendar of Carthage. The rabbis tell a related story of a mother and seven sons under a Roman emperor, in which she tells her youngest to say to Abraham, "You bound one son to the altar, but I bound seven altars" (Bavli Gittin 57b).
